newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta finance minister promises bank law updating.
newsitem.headline: Malta finance minister promises bank law updating.

text.p: Maltese Finance Minister Leo Brincat said on Monday the government would revise the Central Bank of Malta Act to ensure the bank's independence within the context of accountability.
The Act was last updated in late 1994, enabling the bank to make increased use of market-oriented instruments, such as repurchase agreements (repos) in its monetary policy.
The bank was also given the authority to determine the level of lending interest rates.

Brincat, at a conference to mark the 29th anniversary of the Central Bank's creation, gave no details but said the six-month-old Maltese Labour government would also consider reviewing laws on capital markets to encourage greater participation.

"Both the capital and money markets, established in recent years, have registered a notable rise in the volume of business transacted. However, we note with some disappointment that participation in the capital market remains limited.
"While government securities are traded actively on the stock exchange, the number of private sector companies seeking a listing of their shares or bonds remains relatively small," he said.
The government wants to encourage companies to raise equity and longer-term finance on the exchange, he added.
He said: "If the need arises, we will also review existing legislation regulating capital markets to ensure that unnecessary legal obstacles to such participation are removed."
Only six companies have been listed on the Malta exchange. Three are banks and the others are an insurance company, a soft drinks maker and a hotel.
Brincat said the government also intended to strengthen the supervisory function of the Central Bank and the Malta Financial Services Centre.
